transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because over the past year or so, I’ve been getting pulled off task really easily. Like, the smallest thing—a phone buzz, someone walking by my office, or even just some random thought—can derail me before I even catch it.
Thinking back to when you were a child, were you already someone who got distracted easily?

Yeah, looking back, I think so. I remember teachers moving my seat around a lot because I’d talk too much, or I’d get up without asking. I’d also blurt out answers before they even finished asking the question. So yeah, it was there when I was a kid too.
Do these attention problems make it hard for you to keep up with your work?

Yeah, somewhat. I’m still keeping up overall, like things are getting done, but it’s taking more effort than it should. And it’s starting to affect how people deal with me—people at work get impatient when meetings or mentoring conversations don’t go smoothly, and at home it’s started to wear on trust when family plans get thrown off.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
Not really, no. I mean, I get stressed about things when there’s a reason, like work or family stuff, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying a lot for no clear reason.
Do you notice the same distractibility at home as well as at work?

Yeah, it happens in both places. At work it might be my phone buzzing or someone walking by my office, and at home it can be just some random thought, like something with my in-laws, and I’m off track before I even realize it. It’s been more noticeable over the past year or so.
Have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time?
No, not much of the time. I get frustrated or stressed sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling depressed most days.
Do you often feel that you haven’t slept well?
I don’t think so. I mean, some nights aren’t great, but I haven’t really noticed feeling like I don’t sleep well all the time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a persistent pattern of distractibility and childhood-onset hyperactive/impulsive behaviors, with symptoms present across work and home settings and causing functional strain. Anxiety, depression, and sleep problems were not supported as better explanations in the interview. This is most consistent with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, predominantly inattentive presentation under ICD-10 F90.0.
